ptp_clock_identity.description: 64-bit hexadecimal clock identity (e.g., '00:1B:44:00:00:00:00:01'). If left empty, auto-generated.

ptp_domain_number.description: PTP domain number (0–127). All devices in the same domain must use the same value.

ptp_interface.description: Network interface used for PTP traffic. Required for deterministic behavior.

ptp_transport.description: Transport mode: 'udp' (IP-based) or 'l2' (Layer-2 raw Ethernet frames).

ptp_log_level.description: Log verbosity level (0 = all, 7 = none). Recommend 6–7 in production to reduce noise.

ptp_sync_interval.description: Sync message interval exponent. Values: -12 (244 µs) to 3 (8 s). Default -3 (1 s).

ptp_delay_req_interval.description: Delay request interval exponent (optional; defaults to sync_interval if omitted).

ptp_unicast_only.description: If true, ptp4l will only communicate with explicitly configured unicast masters.

ptp_unicast_masters.description: List of allowed unicast master addresses and priorities.

address.description: MAC or IP address of the master (e.g., '00:1B:44:00:00:00:00:02' or '192.168.1.10').

ptp_use_hardware_timestamps.description: Use hardware-assisted PTP timestamping if available. Highly recommended for sub-µs accuracy.

ptp_clock_device.description: Path to the PTP clock device (e.g., /dev/ptp0). Auto-detected if empty.

ptp_max_steps.description: Maximum number of hops (127 = no limit). Reduces convergence speed if set lower.

ptp_boundary_clock_jb.description: If true, operate as a boundary clock (forward messages). Otherwise, ordinary clock.

ptp_slave_only.description: If true, never act as a master—always slave. Useful for endpoint devices.

ptp_accept_any_master.description: If true, accept sync from any master—even those in a different domain.

ptp_sync_loss_timeout.description: Seconds of missed sync before clock goes into unlocked/frozen state. 0 = immediate.

ptp_p2p_delay_req_interval.description: Delay request interval exponent for p2p mode (optional; defaults to sync_interval if omitted).
